French Crypto Worker’s Family Kidnapped at Home, Four Suspects Flee

According to BFMTV, a crypto industry worker, his wife and their two children, aged 8 and 12, were kidnapped and restrained at their home in Vendin-le-Vieil, France. Investigators are considering whether the incident was linked to an attempt to obtain cryptocurrency. The man and his daughter were assaulted, he contacted emergency services at around 8:00 a.m. on Sunday, and the four suspects fled. The amount of any loss remains unknown. — link

ZetaChain Community Votes on Proposal to Migrate ZETA to Solana, with 99.4% Currently in Favor

The ZetaChain community is voting on a proposal to migrate ZETA to Solana. So far, 99.4% of votes are in favor and 0.3% against, with 58% participation, exceeding the 40% quorum requirement. The vote is scheduled to close at around 22:58 Beijing time on Sept. 20. If approved, ZETA will become a native SPL token on Solana, with a 1:1 conversion and unchanged total supply. Anuma, ZetaChain’s private multi-model AI app with more than 300k users, and its Private Memory Layer would also migrate to Solana

Bybit CEO : Bitcoin Is Still Some Way From Becoming Mature “Digital Gold”

On April 15, 2026, Bybit CEO Ben Zhou said in a Cointelegraph interview at Paris Blockchain Week that Bitcoin is still some way from becoming mature “digital gold.” He said its recent volatility remains too high for traditional financial institutions to treat it as a reliable store of value. Meanwhile, Zhou said stablecoins are better suited for everyday payments, without changing Bitcoin’s long-term role as digital gold. — link

WSJ: Polymarket CEO Reportedly Told Staff to Keep Growing and Pay a Fine if Regulators Found Out Amid $10M Stolen-Card Fraud Attempt

The Wall Street Journal reported that fraudsters linked stolen debit cards to Polymarket US accounts in February, attempting to move at least $10 million through wagers and withdrawals. At one point, its payment processor rejected more than 80% of the deposits it handled as fraudulent, far exceeding the industry norm of roughly 1%. According to people familiar with the events, CEO Shayne Coplan's response to employees' concerns was to keep growing and pay a fine

Robinhood Chain Collected $4.5M in Daily Fees, Paid Ethereum Just $400

An analysis published by South Korean outlet Digital Asset highlights the gap between Robinhood Chain’s growth and the economic value captured by Ethereum. According to Bitquery, Robinhood Chain collected approximately $4.5 million in transaction fees on September 3 while paying Ethereum just $398 in data posting and proof costs. The analysis argues that growing Layer 2 activity does not necessarily translate into proportional revenue for Ethereum, as much of the fee revenue remains within the L2 ecosystem. — link
